author: fwyzard
body:
#### PR description: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently, while handing them to the framework in input order. The `StreamerInputSource` event deserialisation is split into a thread-safe decode step (Adler-32 check, decompression, ROOT deserialisation into per-event buffers) and a serial finish step (metadata check, process history, run and lumi auxiliaries). `StreamerFileReader` reads up to `numDecodeTasks` events ahead and decodes them in TBB tasks; whoever claims an event first decodes it, its task or the source, so while events are being processed the source never waits on a `task_group` or runs unrelated tasks. End of file, new event meta data and read errors are handled serially, after all the events read before them have been handed out, so errors are handled in their input order. The new untracked parameter `numDecodeTasks` configures the task parallelism: `1` (default) keeps the current serial behaviour; `N > 1` reads up to N events ahead; `0` uses one slot per framework stream. Each event read ahead keeps its message copy, decompression buffer and deserialised products in memory until the framework takes it, so with `0` the input products need roughly one more copy per stream. Throughput of an input-only job (`GenericConsumer` on all products), 8 threads, AMD EPYC 9534: - 1 MB raw-data events (ZSTD): ~495 ev/s serial, ~2100 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks = 0`; up to ~5000 ev/s with more threads. - 29 kB scouting events: ~2400 ev/s serial, ~8000 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks = 0`; up to ~13000 ev/s. - Run-3 HLT menu on raw-data streamer input, 62 threads: unchanged (~197 ev/s), as the source is not the bottleneck there. #### Performance for Phase 2 HLT inputs (TTbar, pileup 200, skimmed) These plots show the performance of jobs that only read their inputs (with a `source` and a `GenericConsumer` of all the products), using `CMSSW_20_1_0_pre4` with lz4 1.10.0 (cms-sw/cmsdist#10936), the `adler32` optimisation (#52144), reduced process history ids (#52216), LZ4 support for streamer files (#52217), and this PR (#52146), for every compression algorithm and level. The jobs ran on an AMD EPYC 9655 CPU, with 16 physical cores and 32 SMTs, with 32 threads and 32 streams. The plots show the average and standard deviation over three repetitions. _Compression time vs compressed file size_ _Read throughput vs file size_ _Peak memory usage vs read throughput_ With 32 decoding tasks, streamer files compressed with LZ4 are read at 140-146 ev/s, ten times faster than with the serial reads (14 ev/s) and eight times faster than ROOT files with `PoolSource` (17.7 ev/s with `delayReadingEventProducts = False`); ZSTD files are read at 55-66 ev/s, against 12-13 ev/s serially. The price is memory: the peak RSS goes from about 1.3 GB with the serial reads to 4.5-6 GB with 4 tasks and 10-12 GB with 32 tasks. #### Impact on the HLT studies: A measurement of the impact on the Phase 2 HLT performance studies shows that the `NewEventStreamFileReader` with 4 or 8 parallel tasks recovers most of the speed that can be achieved with the `RepeatingCachedRootSource`, using only a fraction of the memory. All results are the average and standard deviation of 4 measurements, on an AMD EPYC 9534 CPU and NVIDIA L40S GPU, using 16 cores, 32 threads and 24 streams : | source | CPU-only throughput | CPU-only peak RSS | GPU offload throughput | GPU offload peak RSS | |---|---|---|---|---| | `RepeatingCachedRootSource` | 6.65 0.01 ev/s | 147.7 0.4 GB | 11.37 0.01 ev/s | 146.9 0.5 GB | | `PoolSource` | 5.88 0.04 ev/s | 20.7 0.4 GB | 7.58 0.08 ev/s | 15.4 0.6 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
serial | 4.74 0.01 ev/s | 18.8 0.5 GB | 5.91 0.01 ev/s | 13.0 0.4 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
4 tasks | 5.60 0.02 ev/s | 25.0 0.5 GB | 9.55 0.01 ev/s | 20.6 0.1 GB | | `NewEventStreamFileReader`
8 tasks | 5.65 0.01 ev/s | 26.0 0.5 GB | 9.61 0.01 ev/s | 22.7 0.2 GB | _Phase 2 HLT running only on CPU_ _Phase 2 HLT running with GPU offload_ #### Notes: - `DQMStreamerReader` and `StreamerInputModule` (used by `WatcherSource`) are not changed: they keep decoding events serially through `deserializeEvent()`, which now calls the new protected `decodeEvent()`/`finishEvent()`. The only internal change is that the `TBufferFile` read buffer is now created per event instead of being a reused member, which costs almost nothing. They could adopt the pipelined decoding in a follow-up. - Skipping events that were already read ahead (`skip()` with a non-empty window) is covered by review only: `skipEvents` is applied before anything is read ahead, and `processingMode = "RunsAndLumis"`, which skips events one by one, already loops forever with `NewEventStreamFileReader` in the release, independently of this PR. #### PR validation: - New unit test `TestIOPoolStreamerPipelined`: serial vs pipelined (`numDecodeTasks` 16 and 0, 1 and 4 threads) on two files, a file with a meta data change in the middle, a file with repeated meta data, `skipEvents`, a truncated last event and a corrupted checksum; with one thread the failing jobs process all the earlier events, as in serial mode. - All `IOPool/Streamer`, `DQMServices/StreamerIO` and `CalibCalorimetry/EcalLaserSorting` unit tests pass. - Re-writing the events with `EventStreamFileWriter` gives byte-identical output with one thread, and the same set of messages with 16 threads, for raw-data and scouting inputs.
title: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently
